title: Autoscale windowed provisioning and iso contract PRD draft
body:
Context and motivation:

We have many overlapping autoscale drafts (predictive warm pools, credit-based bursts, soft-fallbacks). This doc captures a complementary approach: time-windowed provisioning ("windowed provisioning") + explicit tenant isolation contracts (ISO contracts) + a deterministic rollback/credit-escrow protocol. The goal is to provide predictable short-term headroom with strong isolation semantics for regulated/premium tenants while keeping unit-costs low for general purpose tenants.

Why different?
- Most current designs assume continuous reservation or purely reactive autoscaling. Windowed provisioning treats short-term capacity as time-bound leases that are accounted, observable, and reversible.
- ISO contracts formalize the promises we make to Dedicated customers (latency budget windows, fidelity tiers, billing/credits behavior during degradation).
- The escrow/rollback protocol links billing and fidelity so that we can safely do aggressive pre-warm and soft-failovers without customer surprise.

High level idea:
1) Windowed provisioning: allocate small, short-duration capacity windows (e.g. N minutes) that can be booked by tenants ahead-of-time or dynamically by the autoscaler. Windows are pooled by region/hardware class and priced.
2) Escrowed burst credits: when a tenant grabs a window, we place an equivalent credit in escrow. If we fail to deliver promised latency/fidelity during the window we refund or compensate by extra future windows.
3) ISO contracts: customers select a contract that defines: fidelity tier (model variant/quantization), latency budget, acceptable fallback options, and billing/compensation rules. Contracts are machine-readable and enforceable by the routing/autoscaler.
4) Rollback protocol: when capacity strain is detected, the system performs deterministic rollback steps (e.g., ramp fidelity down, route to lower-cost model, degrade non-critical routes) per contract. Rollbacks trigger ledger adjustments in the escrow subsystem and an audit event for SRE/product.

Goals (measurable):
- Provide <1% unexpected SLA violations for ISO-contract tenants during scheduled windows in Q1 pilot.
- Reduce per-token marginal cost for bursty tenants by at least 12% vs continuous warm-pool approach (measured in sim).
- Increase predictability: headroom windows allocated within 30s of request in 90th percentile for autoscaler-assisted bookings.

Non-goals:
- Not meant to replace long-term Reserved Capacity products. This is complementary for short-term surges and regulated guarantees.
- Not a billing overhaul; initial pilot will integrate with existing billing pipes with a small escrow ledger shim.

User stories / personas:
- Platform engineer at a fintech startup: needs a 15-minute block before known monthly statement batch; wants guaranteed latency and audit trail.
- Product manager for a conversational feature: needs on-demand ability to handle marketing campaign surge with predictable billing.
- Enterprise compliance lead: needs ISO contract specifying that PII routes will not fall back to public downstream or lesser-isolated pools.

Key concepts and primitives:
- Window: time-bound capacity lease (start_ts, duration_minute, hw_class, capacity_units).
- Escrow credit: ledger line item mapping tenant -> window -> credit amount; refundable/compensatory rules encoded in contract.
- Fidelity tier: mapping of {model variant, quantization profile, max_seq_len, batching_policy} grouped as P0, P1, P2.
- ISO contract: JSON-ish policy stored in customer profile; consumed by router and autoscaler (examples later).
- Rollback plan: deterministic ordered list of mitigation actions with preconditions, latched to windows and contracts.

Architecture sketch (how pieces interact):
- Booking API (re-use existing quota API): new endpoints to request window reservations (instant or scheduled). Returns window id and escrow token.
- Autoscale controller: manages pools of warm nodes per hw_class and decides whether to accept on-demand windows or decline/queue.
- Router/policy layer: consults ISO contract and window state to decide model variant and region routing for each request.
- Escrow ledger: lightweight service storing window credits and auto-issues refunds/compensations on rollback or missed SLO.
- Observability: per-window spans, SLI measurement and end-of-window reconciliation report.

Example ISO contract snippet (informal):
- fidelity: P0 (unquantized), latency_budget_ms: 120, fallback_allowed: false, billing_policy: partial-refund-on-miss
- fidelity: P1, latency_budget_ms: 200, fallback_allowed: true (to P2), billing_policy: pro-rated-credit

UX / Console changes:
- New "Window bookings" page in Console -> Dedicated -> Reservations. Shows active windows, tenant escrow balance, predicted utilization.
- Contract editor: form-based editor with quick presets (Regulated, Premium, Standard).
- Alerts: per-window SLA miss alert channel + automatic ticket created for SRE if missed > threshold.

APIs (initial):
- POST /dedicated/windows/book {tenant_id, start_ts|null, duration_min, hw_class, fidelity_preference, max_price} -> returns window_id, escrow_token, accepted|queued
- GET /dedicated/windows/{id} -> status, SLI snapshot, route decisions
- POST /dedicated/windows/{id}/cancel -> triggers escrow reconciliation

Telemetry and SLIs:
- window_allocation_latency_p90 (time between request and warmed capacity assigned)
- window_fulfillment_rate (percent of windows where SLI within contract limits)
- per-window_p99_latency, per-window_avg_tokens_per_sec
- escrow_refund_rate and total_refund_amount
- business metric: forecasted vs actual margin impact for windows portfolio

Simulation & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (sim + bench): 4-week sim that adapts historical traffic traces and compares cost/latency vs warm-pool baseline. Success criterion: simulated unit cost improvement >= 8% and fulfillment_rate >= 98% for premium windows.
- Phase 1 (pilot): select 3 existing customers (prod-sim or canary) with predictable surges. Run pilot for 6 weeks. Manual ops guardrails enabled; automatic refunds off for first 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (gradual opt-in): open to all customers with opt-in flag; autoscaler allowed to pre-allocate windows opportunistically; integrate billing refunds.
- Phase 3 (general availability): full integration and minor UI polish.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Detection: per-window SLO drift crosses warning threshold -> page on-call SRE and create ticket.
- Mitigation: follow rollback plan in contract: 1) reduce per-request max tokens, 2) fall back to P2 model if allowed, 3) redirect non-critical routes to public-hosted pool.
- Postmortem: end-of-window reconciliation compares promised SLIs to measured SLIs -> trigger ledger adjustments and generate customer-facing summary email.

Billing implications:
- Escrow ledger holds decimal credits; successful fulfillment drains escrow to normal invoiceable usage; missed SLO issues pro-rated refund.
- Early cancellation penalties configurable per contract (to discourage no-shows after pre-warm cost incurred).

Security & compliance considerations:
- ISO contract may include "no fallback to shared-hosted" flag. Router enforces by denying fallback routes and instead queueing or rejecting requests.
- Audit logs for escrow state and rollback actions retained for 1 year for regulated customers.

Open design questions / risks:
- Pricing model: how to price windows to be attractive vs always-on warm pools? Consider dynamic sliding price per-hour vs fixed credit burn.
- Escrow tax: how to size escrow to cover warm-up cost vs risk of requiring large refunds?
- Complexity: additional cognitive load for customers and ops. Need good defaults and auto-suggestions.
- Edge cases: multi-tenant jobs that span windows; cross-window consistency for KV caches.
- Fraud: customers gaming windows (book -> cancel); need cancellation penalties and behavioral detection.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering: prototype minimal escrow ledger + booking API (Kai) — 3 sprints
- Applied ML: produce fidelity tier mappings (Maya) — 2 sprints
- Infra/SRE: simulate warm-pool vs windowed approach using last 12 months traces (Jonah/Sana) — 4 weeks
- Product: contract presets + console wireframes (Ava) — 2 weeks

Appendix: quick simulation plan
- Dataset: 12 months token-level traces for 10 representative tenants (latency, qps, model variant).
- Scenarios: scheduled surge, unexpected spike, noisy neighbor simultaneous spikes.
- Baselines: existing warm-pool + opportunistic-prewarm + current predictive-autoscaler.
- Metrics to compare: mean marginal cost per token during surge, 95th latency percentile, percent windows fulfilled.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a hybrid operational/product proposal. Looking for feedback on: escrow sizing heuristics, default fidelity presets (P0/P1/P2), and whether we should expose cancellation penalties as a required field in the contract.

Signed-off-by: Ava Martinez (product-dedicated)
